quest.title: For A Better Reunion
quest.description: After all the adventures with the Aranara in the forest, we are getting closer to Bija... Right? Anyway, let's check on Rana first.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x150, Primogem x20, Mora x20000

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Festival Utsava is almost ready to go. It just needs a bit more time!

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: #Yes, it's about to start soon all thanks to Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon's help. I'm really looking forward to the festival...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Araja, Arama, we're back!

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #So happy to see Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon again!

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: #Oh, you're back! Everyone was talking about how a very tall, very powerful Nara named {NICKNAME} helped them out a lot. They were all very happy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #It's always nice to have someone help you out, right, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: No, they're happy because they made new friends. Even if Aranakin, Aranaga, and Aragaru can't remember anymore, the forest will. The story will always live on.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Festival Utsava is almost ready to go. Can't wait!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #You know, we should go check on Rana, {NICKNAME}. Maybe she's better now! If so, we can bring her here!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: I'll go see Arana too, in a while. You guys go ahead!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #See you later, Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon!

choices.text: I'm not getting my hopes up...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Paimon wonders how it compares to the other festivals. Anyway, Paimon's so excited to spend this time with our friends!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If only Rana were here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Rana seems...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon wants to say she's having a sweet dream, but that doesn't sound right...

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: (A blurry image appears in the "bubble" that envelopes Rana.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (You are enthralled by the image.)

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You are in a forest, where everything looks massive and serene. You feel very comfortable here.\nRays of sunshine peek through the sparkling gold leaves, with grass as tall as you swaying quietly all around, gently caressing your hand as you walk by.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You hear the sound of distressed crying amid the musical melody of the wind blowing through the trees and flowing water. Following the sound, you find a small girl.\nShe looks like she has worn herself out from crying and fallen asleep in the meadow. You walk up to her and softly sing a song that can calm all beings...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #...Hey! What's going on, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's glad you're okay... Paimon was so worried... You looked like you were going to pass out...

dialogues.speaker: Arana
dialogues.text: #Nara {NICKNAME}! You're all here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, you freaked Paimon out!

dialogues.speaker: Arana
dialogues.text: Whoa!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Geez, you Aranara! Why are you always spooking people like that!

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: You said "Whoa" first, White Floaty!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's Paimon, not White Floaty!

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: Arana was in the ground to preserve Ararakalari powers. This way, Narana won't wither. But Bija, still needed, for her to be strong again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Okay, Paimon got it. By the way, what just happened to {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Explain the vision you saw.)

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: That should be Arana's memory.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Memory?

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: Oh, let Arana explain. Memories and dreams are Aranara's power, their most precious things. With memories and dreams, Aranara can use Ararakalari to help Nara and Aranara in need of help.

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: #Some Nara can sense the memories in Ararakalari. Nara {NICKNAME} is one of them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds like Ararakalari is something very important! It was you who used Ararakalari to protect Iotham in that cave, right?

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: Yes, it was Arana. Nara Iotham, Nara Kavus, and Nara Sudabeh are all friends, so Arana protected them.

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: We hang out in the forest a lot, so Arana taught them things about the forests and language of the plants. They're very good friends, just like Narana.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: About the missing kids...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right! Before Iotham, Kavus and Sudabeh went missing too, but they were brought back to the village later. Was that also you?

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: Yes. Arana noticed some bad Nara and Nara Valuka taking them, so Arana helped Nara Kavus and Nara Sudabeh run back when the bad Nara weren't looking.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But why couldn't they remember anything?

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: Arana made little Nara sleep and dream, then removed the bad stuff in their dreams. So when they grow, just like saplings growing into big trees, they won't become bad.

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: Otherwise, little Nara would be afraid. If always afraid, they would believe in the power of "fear," and grow up to be scary bad Nara.

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: They're Arana's friends, so Arana didn't want them to become bad Nara.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: They'll grow up to be somebody great! Speaking of which, do you have any clue on the bad Nara trying to take them away?

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: Arana would never forgive them. The bad Nara aren't children of the forest. They bring a group of bad Nara Valuka with them.

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: There is a strange Nara in Vimara Village. He's not a child of the forest, but a child of snow. He looks like a good Nara.

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: He often hangs around the little Nara and they talk about him too. That's why Arana thinks he's good. But Arana has also seen him talking to the bad Nara about Aranara.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In Vimara Village...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How could this be?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah... Paimon doesn't even wanna think about it. People in Vimara Village should treat each other like family... Not to mention that it was that person who caused Rana to become like this...

choices.text: We must go get the bad guy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right. We'll get that person no matter what.

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: #Promise me, Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: Promise that you'll punish that bad Nara, so Nara Iotham, Nara Kavus, and Nara Sudabeh will not be afraid. So that they will grow up like tree sprouts into big, healthy Nara.

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: Narana is all grown up now, so she can't see Arana anymore. But that's okay. Arana is happy knowing she's fine.

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: I haven't played with Narana for a long time. Many suns have risen and set, and many moons have appeared in the sky. Many fruits grew, then returned to the land.

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: Narana grew taller and taller. She was first about Arana's height, and then the size of a small tree. That was when she stopped playing with Arana.

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: Arana told her many stories about the forest. Starshrooms are the reflection of stars from the sky. Seeing the Nilotpala Lotus bloom means you'll be lucky until the next moonrise.

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: Arana will teach Nara Iotham and his friends the same. Arana hopes they will grow up fine like Narana. Oh, but they should not ever run into Marana like Rana did!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Will they forget the encounters when they grow up, just like Rana?

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: Nara Iotham, Nara Kavus, and Nara Sudabeh will also grow up. It's okay if they forget, because in the end, the forest will remember. Nothing will be lost.

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: The forest will remember. No good thing ever fades away. All pains will become the nourishment of something beautiful...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Arana! Nara {NICKNAME}! Paimon!

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: Arama! Arana hasn't seen you for quite a while!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Come on, Paimon doesn't freak out that easy!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you coming to get us to celebrate Festival Utsava at Vanarana?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Yes! It's ready now, and everyone's waiting for Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hooray! Festival Utsava! Arana, aren't you coming with us?

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: Arana will not go. If Arana is away for too long, Ararakalari won't hold up and Narana will be in danger. So, no festival for Arana.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohh...

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: #It's okay, as long as Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon are happy, so will Arana, Arama, and everyone at Vanarana.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Yeah. The Bija needs you, Arana.

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: Arana will be ready by then.

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: #Oh, this is for you, Nara {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A flower...?

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: Yes. Please take good care of her.

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: #Thank you, Nara {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Let's get back then, Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon!

choices.text: Are we going back for Festival Utsava?
Someone's out to get the kids?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: They'll grow up to be somebody great! Speaking of which, do you have any clue on the bad Nara trying to take them away?

choices.text: I'm sure I've seen this scene before...

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #Arama will go see Arana in a while, too. You guys go ahead! See you later, Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: See you later, Arana!

dialogues.speaker: Arana
dialogues.text: See you later!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Araja, Arama, we're back!

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #So happy to see Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon again!

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: #Oh, you're back! Everyone was talking about how a very tall, very powerful Nara named {NICKNAME} helped them out a lot. They were all very happy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #It's always nice to have someone help you out, right, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: No, they're happy because they made new friends. Even if Aranakin, Aranaga, and Aragaru can't remember anymore, the forest will. The story will always live on.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Festival Utsava is almost ready to go. It just needs a bit more time!

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: #Yes, it's about to start soon, all thanks to Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon's help. I'm really looking forward to the festival...

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: Festival Utsava which was once told of in my story... Will I be able to experience it again myself?

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Let's get back to Vanarana!

dialogues.speaker: Arana
dialogues.text: #Enjoy Festival Utsava, Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon! Everyone will be even more delighted if they see you having fun!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I still have some things I have to do...

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Sure! Let me know when you're ready!
